set1.io: Objective a — Etiologies, epidemiology, risk factors, manifestations, differential diagnosis, testing, management, referrals, education and prognosis for cutaneous bacterial infections
set1.q: What level of the skin does impetigo infect, and which organisms cause it?
opts: An infection of the upper dermis and superficial lymphatics, most often Streptococcus pyogenes
That describes erysipelas.
An infection of the deeper dermis and subcutaneous tissue, streptococcal or staphylococcal
That describes cellulitis.
An infection of the tissue surrounding muscle and fascia, usually polymicrobial in nature
That describes necrotizing fasciitis.
A superficial epidermal infection, most often Staphylococcus aureus or Streptococcus pyogenes
Correct. It is very contagious and autoinoculable, and common in infants and children.

set1.io: Objective a — Etiologies, epidemiology, risk factors, manifestations, differential diagnosis, testing, management, referrals, education and prognosis for cutaneous bacterial infections
set1.q: How does acute post-streptococcal glomerulonephritis present after impetigo?
opts: Gradual weight loss, painless jaundice, pale stools and dark urine over several weeks
That picture is unrelated to this complication.
Fever with a sandpaper rash, strawberry tongue and circumoral pallor within days
That describes scarlet fever rather than this renal complication.
Migratory joint pain, a new heart murmur and subcutaneous nodules over the elbows
That describes acute rheumatic fever.
Sudden oedema, haematuria with smoky or tea-coloured urine, proteinuria and hypertension
Correct, especially in three to seven year olds.

set1.io: Objective a — Etiologies, epidemiology, risk factors, manifestations, differential diagnosis, testing, management, referrals, education and prognosis for cutaneous bacterial infections
set1.q: What is a furuncle?
opts: A deep-seated abscess of a hair follicle and the adjacent subcutaneous tissue
Correct. Staphylococcus aureus is the commonest organism.
An inflammation of the follicle wall and ostia forming a superficial pustule
That is folliculitis, which is confined to the follicle.
A collection of purulent material seeded by traumatic inoculation of bacteria
That is an abscess, which arises from inoculation rather than a follicle.
An infection of the upper dermis extending into superficial skin lymphatics
That is erysipelas.

set1.io: Objective a — Etiologies, epidemiology, risk factors, manifestations, differential diagnosis, testing, management, referrals, education and prognosis for cutaneous bacterial infections
set1.q: Which topical agent is an alternative comedolytic for patients who cannot tolerate a retinoid?
opts: Dapsone gel, an anti-inflammatory with an unknown mechanism
Dapsone gel is not described as a comedolytic agent.
Salicylic acid, a beta-hydroxy acid that is oil-soluble
Correct. It softens keratin and dissolves the debris that clogs pores.
Benzoyl peroxide, a topical antimicrobial and keratolytic
It is first line for mild acne but is not the named retinoid alternative.
Clindamycin, a topical antimicrobial active against the follicle
Topical antimicrobials are explicitly described as not comedolytic.

set1.io: Objective a — Etiologies, epidemiology, risk factors, manifestations, differential diagnosis, testing, management, referrals, education and prognosis for cutaneous bacterial infections
set1.q: Why may an area of necrotizing fasciitis stop being tender as the disease advances?
opts: The antibiotic has reached therapeutic levels
Devitalised tissue is not perfused by antibiotics at all.
The superficial nerves have been destroyed
Correct, alongside skin colour change to blue-grey, bullae and cutaneous gangrene.
The inflammatory response has begun to resolve
Loss of tenderness here signals progression rather than recovery.
The infection has been contained by the fascia
The fascial planes are what the infection spreads along.

set1.io: Objective d — Medical care strategies across infant, adolescent, adult and elderly populations
set1.q: What isolation advice is given for a child with impetigo?
opts: Isolate until every crusted lesion has completely healed and the skin is clear
The stated interval is tied to starting treatment, not to healing.
No isolation is needed at any point, since impetigo does not spread person to person
Impetigo is described as very contagious and autoinoculable.
Isolate for a full ten days from the appearance of the very first crusted lesion
That is longer than the interval given.
Isolate until treatment has been underway for twenty-four to forty-eight hours
Correct, and do not share towels, clothing, bath water, washcloths or razors.

set1.io: Objective a — Etiologies, epidemiology, risk factors, manifestations, differential diagnosis, testing, management, referrals, education and prognosis for cutaneous bacterial infections
set1.q: Where does erythrasma most commonly appear?
opts: Inner thighs, crural region, scrotum, and between the fourth and fifth toes
Correct. Less common sites are the axilla, under the breasts and intergluteal folds.
Back of the neck, face, axillae and buttocks, favouring areas of friction
That is the distribution of furuncles and carbuncles.
Face and extremities, spreading by scratching and self-inoculation
That is the distribution of non-bullous impetigo.
Lower extremity in most patients, almost never affecting both legs
That is the distribution of cellulitis.

set1.io: Objective a — Etiologies, epidemiology, risk factors, manifestations, differential diagnosis, testing, management, referrals, education and prognosis for cutaneous bacterial infections
set1.q: How does chronic paronychia present, and over what timescale?
opts: Grouped painful vesicles on the distal finger appearing over twenty-four hours
That describes herpetic whitlow.
Oedematous, erythematous, tender nail folds without fluctuance, present at least six weeks
Correct. Nail plates thicken and discolour, and cuticles separate from the plate.
Rapid onset of erythema and swelling two to five days after trauma, often fluctuant
That describes acute paronychia.
Painless thickening and yellowing of the nail plate over months without inflammation
That describes onychomycosis.

set1.io: Objective b — Unique considerations of methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus skin infections
set1.q: How does purulence change the antibiotic choice in cellulitis?
opts: Purulent cellulitis prompts topical mupirocin in addition to the oral antibiotic
Topical mupirocin is used in impetigo and for nasal decolonisation.
Purulent cellulitis prompts oral fluconazole because yeast is likely to be present
Antifungal therapy belongs to chronic paronychia.
Purulent cellulitis prompts cover for methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus
Correct — trimethoprim-sulfamethoxazole, doxycycline, clindamycin or linezolid.
Purulent cellulitis prompts a switch to penicillin V to cover Group A streptococcus
Penicillin V is the erysipelas treatment.

set1.io: Objective d — Medical care strategies across infant, adolescent, adult and elderly populations
set1.q: Which oral antibiotic is described as the drug of choice for impetigo in children?
opts: Dicloxacillin
It is listed as an option but not the paediatric drug of choice.
Erythromycin
It is not the agent named for children here.
Cephalexin
Correct. Clindamycin is used where there is penicillin allergy.
Doxycycline
Doxycycline is limited to children over eight years old.

set1.io: Objective a — Etiologies, epidemiology, risk factors, manifestations, differential diagnosis, testing, management, referrals, education and prognosis for cutaneous bacterial infections
set1.q: What does the 2016 American Academy of Dermatology guideline recommend for comedonal acne?
opts: A topical retinoid with an oral antibiotic and topical benzoyl peroxide together
That is the recommendation for moderate papulopustular and mixed acne.
Oral isotretinoin as monotherapy over a sixteen to twenty week treatment course
That is an option for severe nodular acne.
A topical retinoid, switching to azelaic or salicylic acid if it is not tolerated
Correct. That is the entry point of the treatment ladder.
A topical antimicrobial with a topical retinoid, or benzoyl peroxide with an antibiotic
That is the recommendation for mild papulopustular and mixed acne.

set1.io: Objective a — Etiologies, epidemiology, risk factors, manifestations, differential diagnosis, testing, management, referrals, education and prognosis for cutaneous bacterial infections
set1.q: Which risk factors are named for necrotizing fasciitis?
opts: Manicure, hangnail, ingrown nail and the habit of biting or picking at the nails
Those are predisposing factors for acute paronychia.
Trauma, burns, surgery, immunosuppression, renal failure, alcoholism, dental infection and injection drug use
Correct, and it occurs more often in males than females.
Obesity, poor hygiene, occlusive clothing, hot humid weather and nasal staphylococcal carriage
Those are the risk factors for folliculitis.
Mastectomy, tinea pedis, obesity and any pre-existing superficial skin infection
Those are the risk factors for erysipelas.

set1.io: Objective a — Etiologies, epidemiology, risk factors, manifestations, differential diagnosis, testing, management, referrals, education and prognosis for cutaneous bacterial infections
set1.q: Which three elements are required to diagnose hidradenitis suppurativa?
opts: Coral-red fluorescence under a Wood's lamp, intertriginous distribution, and a history of diabetes mellitus
That fluorescence is the diagnostic finding in erythrasma.
Typical lesions, characteristic distribution in axilla and groin, and recurrence more than twice in six months
Correct. It is primarily a clinical diagnosis; biopsy is not usually required.
Positive bacterial culture, characteristic distribution over the trunk, and failure of oral antibiotic therapy
Culture and treatment failure are not part of the diagnostic criteria.
A biopsy showing apocrine gland destruction, raised inflammatory markers, and a family history of disease
Biopsy is not usually required to make the diagnosis.

set1.io: Objective a — Etiologies, epidemiology, risk factors, manifestations, differential diagnosis, testing, management, referrals, education and prognosis for cutaneous bacterial infections
set1.q: What is the typical timing and distribution of hot tub folliculitis?
opts: Onset within forty-eight hours, on the lower extremity with a demarcated border
That describes erysipelas.
Onset three to seven days after a sore throat, on the face and extremities
That timing belongs to post-streptococcal glomerulonephritis after impetigo.
Onset eight hours to five days after exposure, on the trunk, extremities and buttocks
Correct. It usually spares the face, neck, soles and palms.
Onset two to five days after trauma, around the fingernail folds of the hand
That is the timing and site of acute paronychia.

set1.io: Objective a — Etiologies, epidemiology, risk factors, manifestations, differential diagnosis, testing, management, referrals, education and prognosis for cutaneous bacterial infections
set1.q: How is a cutaneous abscess treated?
opts: Warm compresses alone in every case, since abscesses reliably resolve without any intervention
That approach suits small furuncles rather than abscesses.
Wide surgical excision of the affected area, since recurrence is otherwise close to universal
Wide excision belongs to hidradenitis suppurativa.
Surgical incision and drainage if it does not drain spontaneously; warm soaks and antibiotics if it does
Correct. Broad-spectrum cover considers methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus, then narrows to culture.
Oral antibiotics alone in every case, since incision risks spreading the infection into the blood
Incision and drainage is the treatment when it does not drain on its own.

set1.io: Objective a — Etiologies, epidemiology, risk factors, manifestations, differential diagnosis, testing, management, referrals, education and prognosis for cutaneous bacterial infections
set1.q: How is acne vulgaris diagnosed?
opts: By bacterial culture of a pustule taken before treatment begins
Culture is only considered when treatment fails.
By punch biopsy of an inflammatory lesion sent for histology
Biopsy has no role in the routine diagnosis of acne.
By measuring serum androgens in every patient at presentation
Hormonal testing is directed by clinical suspicion, not routine.
Clinically, with culture reserved for cases that fail to respond
Correct. No routine test is needed to make the diagnosis.

set1.io: Objective a — Etiologies, epidemiology, risk factors, manifestations, differential diagnosis, testing, management, referrals, education and prognosis for cutaneous bacterial infections
set1.q: What should be suspected when acne scarring seems out of proportion to the severity of lesions?
opts: Patient manipulation of the lesions through picking or squeezing
Correct. Patients and families are educated about that risk.
An undiagnosed hyperandrogenic state driving deeper inflammation
Hyperandrogenism is suspected from hirsutism and menstrual irregularity.
Resistance of Cutibacterium acnes to the prescribed antimicrobial
Resistance would show as failure to improve, not disproportionate scarring.
An underlying immunodeficiency impairing the healing of each lesion
That is not among the explanations the lecture offers.

set1.io: Objective a — Etiologies, epidemiology, risk factors, manifestations, differential diagnosis, testing, management, referrals, education and prognosis for cutaneous bacterial infections
set1.q: What is the expected course of cellulitis on antibiotic therapy?
opts: It may look worse on day one, fever usually resolves within twenty-four hours, inflammation over one to two weeks
Correct. Fever beyond forty-eight hours prompts a change guided by culture.
It improves visibly within hours, fever resolves within six hours, and erythema clears within three days
That is faster than the described course.
It worsens for the first week before any improvement, with fever expected to persist throughout
Fever persisting beyond forty-eight hours is a reason to change therapy.
It resolves without any change in appearance, since the erythema is not caused by the infection
The erythema is part of the infection.

set1.io: Objective b — Unique considerations of methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus skin infections
set1.q: When should cultures be obtained in impetigo?
opts: When the patient is at high risk for methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus, or when post-streptococcal glomerulonephritis is present
Correct — a health-care worker or teacher is the example given of high risk.
In every case at first presentation, since staphylococcal and streptococcal disease are treated differently from one another
Impetigo is most often diagnosed by clinical appearance alone.
Only when the lesions have failed to respond after a full two-week course of topical mupirocin
Culture is directed by resistance risk and complications, not treatment duration.
Only in children under three years of age, since they are the group at highest risk of complications
Post-streptococcal glomerulonephritis particularly affects three to seven year olds.

set1.io: Objective a — Etiologies, epidemiology, risk factors, manifestations, differential diagnosis, testing, management, referrals, education and prognosis for cutaneous bacterial infections
set1.q: Which oral antibiotics are most commonly used for acne, and what is used when they are contraindicated?
opts: Doxycycline and minocycline, with erythromycin when a tetracycline is contraindicated
Correct. Sarecycline, a tetracycline derivative, was approved in 2018 for moderate to severe acne.
Cephalexin and dicloxacillin, with clindamycin when a penicillin is contraindicated
That is the antibiotic pairing for folliculitis and furuncles.
Erythromycin and clarithromycin, with miconazole when a macrolide is contraindicated
That combination is used for widespread erythrasma.
Penicillin V and amoxicillin, with azithromycin when a penicillin is contraindicated
Penicillin V is the treatment named for erysipelas.

set1.io: Objective a — Etiologies, epidemiology, risk factors, manifestations, differential diagnosis, testing, management, referrals, education and prognosis for cutaneous bacterial infections
set1.q: What is acute paronychia and what predisposes to it?
opts: Viral infection of the distal finger producing grouped vesicles on an erythematous base
That describes herpetic whitlow, also a differential.
Infection of the soft tissue around the fingernail, from manicure, ingrown nail, hangnail or nail biting
Correct. It starts as cellulitis and progresses to abscess; Staphylococcus aureus and Streptococcus pyogenes are typical.
Inflammation of the proximal nail fold from irritants and allergens, in cleaners, cooks and bartenders
That describes chronic paronychia.
Infection of the fingertip pulp space producing throbbing pain and a tense, swollen finger pad
That describes a felon, listed among the differentials.

set1.io: Objective c — Differentiate primary from secondary bacterial infection of the skin
set1.q: Which portals of entry are named for cellulitis?
opts: Manicure, ingrown nail, hangnail and nail biting affecting the soft tissue of the finger
Those are predisposing factors for acute paronychia.
Contaminated whirlpools, hot tubs, water slides and inadequately chlorinated pools
Those are the exposures for Pseudomonas folliculitis.
Tinea pedis, open lesion, trauma, surgical wound, insect bite, fissure and radiation therapy
Correct. Those are distinct from the risk factors, which include diabetes and lymphoedema.
Nasal carriage of Staphylococcus aureus, shaving, occlusive clothing and hot humid weather
Those are risk factors for folliculitis and furuncles.

set1.io: Objective a — Etiologies, epidemiology, risk factors, manifestations, differential diagnosis, testing, management, referrals, education and prognosis for cutaneous bacterial infections
set1.q: How does erysipelas present systemically?
opts: Sudden onset of malaise, myalgias, chills and high fever within forty-eight hours of skin changes
Correct, with nausea, headache, pruritus, burning, tenderness and swelling.
Gradual onset of low-grade fever and fatigue over the two weeks before the rash appears
The onset is described as sudden, not gradual.
No systemic symptoms at all, with the patient consistently afebrile and otherwise well
That describes folliculitis.
Unrelenting pain out of proportion to examination, with skin colour changing to blue-grey
That describes necrotizing fasciitis.

set1.io: Objective a — Etiologies, epidemiology, risk factors, manifestations, differential diagnosis, testing, management, referrals, education and prognosis for cutaneous bacterial infections
set1.q: How is chronic paronychia treated?
opts: Warm soaks three times daily with incision and drainage if purulent material has collected
That is the treatment of acute paronychia.
Oral cephalexin for ten days with removal of the nail plate if there is no early response
Antibacterial therapy does not address the usual candidal cause.
Topical mupirocin applied to the nail fold three times daily until the swelling settles
Mupirocin is an antibacterial used for impetigo and staphylococcal carriage.
Keep the hands dry and use a broad-spectrum topical antifungal, with oral fluconazole in severe cases
Correct — treat the underlying inflammation and infection together.

set1.io: Objective a — Etiologies, epidemiology, risk factors, manifestations, differential diagnosis, testing, management, referrals, education and prognosis for cutaneous bacterial infections
set1.q: What defines folliculitis?
opts: Inflammatory cells within the wall and ostia of the hair follicle, forming a follicular pustule
Correct. The causes include infection, physical injury and chemical irritation.
A deep-seated abscess of the hair follicle and the adjacent subcutaneous tissue
That defines a furuncle.
Inflammation of the cutaneous apocrine glands of the axilla, groin or perineum
That defines hidradenitis suppurativa.
A foreign body reaction to a cut hair that curves back into the wall of the follicle
That defines pseudofolliculitis barbae.

set1.io: Objective a — Etiologies, epidemiology, risk factors, manifestations, differential diagnosis, testing, management, referrals, education and prognosis for cutaneous bacterial infections
set1.q: When are oral antibiotics indicated in acne vulgaris?
opts: For patients with acne scarring, in order to prevent any further scars from developing over time
Scarring is not the stated indication for systemic antibiotics.
For moderate to severe acne too widespread for topicals, or after an inadequate response over six to eight weeks
Correct, and they are prescribed for the shortest time possible, about three to four months.
For comedonal acne at first presentation, before any topical therapy has been trialled at all
Comedonal acne is treated with a topical retinoid first.
For any patient whose acne has failed to clear completely within two weeks of starting treatment
Improvement in lesions takes four to six weeks.

set1.io: Objective a — Etiologies, epidemiology, risk factors, manifestations, differential diagnosis, testing, management, referrals, education and prognosis for cutaneous bacterial infections
set1.q: What does the 2016 guideline recommend for severe nodular acne?
opts: A topical retinoid alone, switching to azelaic or salicylic acid if it is not tolerated
That is the recommendation for comedonal acne.
Benzoyl peroxide with a topical antibiotic and no retinoid at any stage of treatment
That option exists only for mild disease where a retinoid is not tolerated.
An oral contraceptive pill with spironolactone as the initial approach in all patients
Hormonal therapy is considered for hyperandrogenism or unresponsive disease.
A topical retinoid with an oral antibiotic and benzoyl peroxide, or isotretinoin monotherapy
Correct. Moderate disease gets the same triple combination without the isotretinoin alternative.

set1.io: Objective b — Unique considerations of methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus skin infections
set1.q: Which measure is recommended when methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus is a concern in a drained furuncle?
opts: Start linezolid empirically before any material is obtained
Empiric therapy uses dicloxacillin or cephalexin unless resistance is suspected.
Swab the nasal vestibule of every household contact first
Nasal swabbing is described for recurrent folliculitis.
Defer drainage until the culture result becomes available
Drainage is not delayed for culture.
Culture the material obtained at incision and drainage
Correct, and give endocarditis prophylaxis to at-risk patients.

set1.io: Objective a — Etiologies, epidemiology, risk factors, manifestations, differential diagnosis, testing, management, referrals, education and prognosis for cutaneous bacterial infections
set1.q: Which shaving advice is given for pseudofolliculitis barbae?
opts: Continue the current routine and treat each papule with a topical antibiotic
The shaving technique itself has to change.
Stop shaving if possible, use clean razors, and avoid lift-and-cut razor systems
Correct — mild razor angles and single or at most double blades are preferred.
Shave daily against the grain with a multi-blade razor to cut hairs below the surface
Cutting hair below the surface is what allows it to re-enter the skin.
Shave weekly with an electric razor set to the closest possible cutting length
The closest cut is the problem rather than the solution.

set1.io: Objective a — Etiologies, epidemiology, risk factors, manifestations, differential diagnosis, testing, management, referrals, education and prognosis for cutaneous bacterial infections
set1.q: Which single clue is emphasised for recognising necrotizing fasciitis early?
opts: Honey-coloured crusting over a superficial epidermal erosion
That finding points to non-bullous impetigo.
Coral-red fluorescence of the affected skin under a Wood's lamp
That finding points to erythrasma.
Unrelenting pain out of proportion to the physical examination
Correct — patients are often diagnosed with cellulitis, sent home, and return worse.
A sharply demarcated plaque raised above the surrounding skin
That finding points to erysipelas.

set2.io: Objective a — Etiologies, epidemiology, risk factors, manifestations, differential diagnosis, testing, management, referrals, education and prognosis for cutaneous bacterial infections
set2.q: Describe the classic appearance of non-bullous impetigo.
opts: A macule evolves into a vesicle or pustule that ruptures, leaving a honey-coloured adherent crust
Correct, typically on the face and extremities, with regional lymphadenopathy common.
Tense clear or cloudy bullae appear on intact skin and leave a collarette after they rupture
That is bullous impetigo.
A vesicle over inflamed skin deepens into a dermal ulcer with a thick grey-yellow crust
That is ecthyma.
Papules and pustules on an erythematous base, each pierced by a single central hair
That is folliculitis.

set2.io: Objective a — Etiologies, epidemiology, risk factors, manifestations, differential diagnosis, testing, management, referrals, education and prognosis for cutaneous bacterial infections
set2.q: What distinguishes ecthyma from ordinary impetigo?
opts: It spreads rapidly along superficial lymphatics with a sharply demarcated raised edge
That describes erysipelas.
It deepens into a dermal ulceration with a thicker grey-yellow crust, heals slowly and scars
Correct, usually on the lower extremities, with regional lymphadenopathy common.
It remains confined to the epidermis, resolves within a week and never leaves a scar behind
That describes ordinary impetigo rather than ecthyma.
It produces tense bullae on intact skin that rupture to leave shallow moist erosions
That describes bullous impetigo.

set2.io: Objective b — Unique considerations of methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus skin infections
set2.q: Which oral agents are named for folliculitis when methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus is cultured or suspected?
opts: Cephalexin, dicloxacillin or amoxicillin-clavulanate
Those cover methicillin-sensitive disease rather than the resistant organism.
Penicillin V, clindamycin or erythromycin base
Penicillin V is the erysipelas treatment.
Doxycycline, minocycline or sarecycline
Those are the oral tetracyclines used in acne.
Trimethoprim-sulfamethoxazole, ciprofloxacin or linezolid
Correct. Cephalexin and dicloxacillin cover the methicillin-sensitive organism.

set2.io: Objective a — Etiologies, epidemiology, risk factors, manifestations, differential diagnosis, testing, management, referrals, education and prognosis for cutaneous bacterial infections
set2.q: Which oral antibiotic is specifically suggested for paronychia after nail biting?
opts: Clindamycin, because of exposure to oral flora
Correct. Amoxicillin-clavulanate and cephalexin are the other named options.
Doxycycline, because of exposure to oral flora
Doxycycline is not the agent named for this exposure.
Ciprofloxacin, because of exposure to oral flora
Ciprofloxacin is named for resistant Pseudomonas folliculitis.
Penicillin V, because of exposure to oral flora
Penicillin V is the erysipelas treatment.

set2.io: Objective a — Etiologies, epidemiology, risk factors, manifestations, differential diagnosis, testing, management, referrals, education and prognosis for cutaneous bacterial infections
set2.q: What is the treatment of necrotizing fasciitis?
opts: Warm compresses with elevation of the limb and a narrow-spectrum oral antibiotic course
That is far below the level of care this condition requires.
Aggressive surgical debridement with broad antibiotic cover and surgical intensive care admission
Correct — cover aerobic Gram-positive and Gram-negative organisms and anaerobes, with a team approach.
Broad intravenous antibiotics alone with observation on a general medical ward for forty-eight hours
Antibiotics alone are inadequate; debridement is required.
Incision and drainage under local anaesthetic followed by discharge on oral antibiotics
That approach belongs to a simple abscess.

set2.io: Objective a — Etiologies, epidemiology, risk factors, manifestations, differential diagnosis, testing, management, referrals, education and prognosis for cutaneous bacterial infections
set2.q: Why should topical tretinoin and benzoyl peroxide not be applied at the same time?
opts: Because tretinoin blocks the antimicrobial effect that benzoyl peroxide has
No such interaction is described.
Because of the risk of skin irritation, so at least three hours should separate them
Correct. That interval is specified in the patient education.
Because benzoyl peroxide inactivates tretinoin, so alternate days are recommended
Irritation, not inactivation, is the stated reason.
Because the combination raises the risk of photosensitivity in treated areas
Sun sensitivity is a separate caution about acne treatments generally.

set2.io: Objective a — Etiologies, epidemiology, risk factors, manifestations, differential diagnosis, testing, management, referrals, education and prognosis for cutaneous bacterial infections
set2.q: How is erythrasma treated?
opts: Dilute acetic acid compresses if localised, oral ciprofloxacin if the disease is widespread
That is the treatment for Pseudomonas folliculitis.
Topical antifungal alone if localised, oral fluconazole if the disease proves severe
That is the treatment for chronic paronychia.
Topical erythromycin or clindamycin if localised, oral erythromycin or clarithromycin if widespread
Correct. An antifungal cream such as miconazole is added if yeast is also present.
Topical mupirocin if localised, oral dicloxacillin or cephalexin if the disease is widespread
That is the treatment ladder for impetigo.

set2.io: Objective a — Etiologies, epidemiology, risk factors, manifestations, differential diagnosis, testing, management, referrals, education and prognosis for cutaneous bacterial infections
set2.q: By what mechanisms do oral contraceptive pills improve acne?
opts: Progestin blocks the androgen receptor within the sebaceous gland and reduces keratinisation
That is not the mechanism the lecture describes.
Estrogen suppresses Cutibacterium acnes directly and reduces follicular hyperkeratinisation
Those are the actions of antimicrobials and retinoids respectively.
Estrogen decreases sebum, suppresses ovarian androgens and raises sex hormone binding globulin
Correct. Raising that globulin lowers circulating free testosterone.
Estrogen increases sebum, stimulates ovarian androgens and lowers sex hormone binding globulin
Every clause reverses the actual effect.

set2.io: Objective a — Etiologies, epidemiology, risk factors, manifestations, differential diagnosis, testing, management, referrals, education and prognosis for cutaneous bacterial infections
set2.q: What are the examination findings of cellulitis?
opts: Tense bullae with purple fluid and skin that has become insensate over the affected area
Those are the late findings of necrotizing fasciitis.
All four cardinal signs of inflammation, most often on one lower leg, with borders neither raised nor demarcated
Correct. Bilateral disease is described as almost never occurring.
All four cardinal signs of inflammation, most often bilateral, with a sharply raised and demarcated edge
A raised demarcated border points to erysipelas, and bilateral disease is atypical.
Painless erythema with scaling at the border, most often over intertriginous skin surfaces
That picture suggests a dermatophyte infection instead.

set2.io: Objective b — Unique considerations of methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus skin infections
set2.q: Which oral antibiotics are used for furuncles and carbuncles when methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus is cultured or suspected?
opts: Ciprofloxacin, levofloxacin or moxifloxacin
Ciprofloxacin is named for resistant Pseudomonas folliculitis.
Trimethoprim-sulfamethoxazole, clindamycin or doxycycline
Correct. Empiric therapy for the sensitive organism is dicloxacillin or cephalexin.
Dicloxacillin, cephalexin or amoxicillin-clavulanate
Those are the empiric agents for methicillin-sensitive disease.
Penicillin V, erythromycin or clarithromycin
Penicillin V is used for erysipelas and the macrolides for erythrasma.

set2.io: Objective b — Unique considerations of methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus skin infections
set2.q: Which patients are given as examples of high risk for methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus in the impetigo section?
opts: A health-care worker or a teacher
Correct. Culture is obtained in those patients rather than in every case.
A child under three or an infant
Age alone is not the example given for resistance risk.
A swimmer or a laundry worker
Those occupations predispose to chronic paronychia.
A bartender or a professional cook
Those occupations also predispose to chronic paronychia.

set2.io: Objective a — Etiologies, epidemiology, risk factors, manifestations, differential diagnosis, testing, management, referrals, education and prognosis for cutaneous bacterial infections
set2.q: Which intervention offers the best chance of permanent cure in hidradenitis suppurativa?
opts: Long-term systemic antibiotic therapy
Long-term outcomes with systemic antibiotics are often poor.
Intralesional triamcinolone injections
Those decrease the size of draining sinuses rather than cure.
Infliximab given for severe disease
That is used for disease unresponsive to corticosteroids.
Wide excision of the affected areas
Correct. Large fluctuant cysts are meanwhile incised and drained.

set2.io: Objective a — Etiologies, epidemiology, risk factors, manifestations, differential diagnosis, testing, management, referrals, education and prognosis for cutaneous bacterial infections
set2.q: Why is spironolactone used in hidradenitis suppurativa?
opts: It is an immunosuppressant that blocks tumour necrosis factor in inflamed tissue
That is the mechanism of infliximab.
It is a retinoid that reduces sebum production and follicular hyperkeratinisation
That is oral isotretinoin, also used in this condition.
It is a corticosteroid that shrinks draining sinuses when injected into a lesion
That is intralesional triamcinolone acetonide.
It is an aldosterone antagonist that inhibits ovarian and adrenal androgen production
Correct. Combination birth control pills act by reducing gonadotropin release.

set2.io: Objective d — Medical care strategies across infant, adolescent, adult and elderly populations
set2.q: How does the sex distribution of acne differ between adolescence and adulthood?
opts: Adolescent acne is more common and severe in males; post-adolescent acne is more common in women
Correct. Post-adolescent acne is defined here as acne over 25 years of age.
Adolescent acne is more common and severe in females; post-adolescent acne is more common in men
That reverses both halves of the stated pattern.
Adolescent acne affects both sexes equally; post-adolescent acne is far more common in men
Adolescent disease is specifically described as more common and severe in males.
Adolescent acne is more common in males; post-adolescent acne affects both sexes about equally
Post-adolescent acne is specifically more common in women than men.

set2.io: Objective a — Etiologies, epidemiology, risk factors, manifestations, differential diagnosis, testing, management, referrals, education and prognosis for cutaneous bacterial infections
set2.q: What is the hallmark lesion of acne vulgaris on physical examination?
opts: The pustule, sitting on an erythematous base around a central hair
That is the lesion of folliculitis.
The nodule, deep-seated and arising in several adjacent follicles
Nodules occur in acne but the hallmark is the comedone.
The papule, small and inflamed without any surface keratin plug
Papules occur in acne but they are not what defines it.
The comedone, either open (blackhead) or closed (whitehead)
Correct. Acne is polymorphic, but the comedone is what defines it.

set2.io: Objective a — Etiologies, epidemiology, risk factors, manifestations, differential diagnosis, testing, management, referrals, education and prognosis for cutaneous bacterial infections
set2.q: Which preventive measures are advised in hidradenitis suppurativa?
opts: Avoid all water contact, apply a barrier ointment daily, gain weight and use an occlusive dressing
None of those measures is recommended for this condition.
Shower immediately after any hot tub use and monitor the disinfectant levels in the water
Those are the preventive measures for Pseudomonas folliculitis.
Avoid sharing towels or razors and isolate from school until treatment has been underway
Those are the patient education points for impetigo.
Avoid heat, cleanse daily with antibacterial soap or benzoyl peroxide wash, lose weight, stop smoking
Correct, along with avoiding constrictive clothing and considering laser hair removal.

set2.io: Objective a — Etiologies, epidemiology, risk factors, manifestations, differential diagnosis, testing, management, referrals, education and prognosis for cutaneous bacterial infections
set2.q: Describe the physical findings of a carbuncle.
opts: Nodules, sinus tracts and meshlike scarring in the axilla or the perineum
That describes hidradenitis suppurativa.
A well-demarcated raised plaque with red streaks extending toward a lymph node
That describes erysipelas with lymphatic involvement.
Several loculated abscesses, superficial pustules, necrotic plugs and sieve-like draining openings
Correct — a deeper infection made of interconnecting furuncles in several follicles.
A single firm tender nodule with one opening and a surrounding zone of erythema and swelling
That is the furuncle rather than the carbuncle.

set2.io: Objective a — Etiologies, epidemiology, risk factors, manifestations, differential diagnosis, testing, management, referrals, education and prognosis for cutaneous bacterial infections
set2.q: Which layer does erysipelas involve, and which organism causes it?
opts: The upper dermis and superficial cutaneous lymphatics, most often Group A streptococcus
Correct. It is a superficial cellulitis of the dermal layer.
The deeper dermis and subcutaneous tissue, most often Staphylococcus aureus
That describes cellulitis rather than erysipelas.
The superficial epidermis only, most often Streptococcus pyogenes or staphylococci
That describes impetigo.
The fascia surrounding muscle and nerve, most often a polymicrobial mixture
That describes necrotizing fasciitis.

set2.io: Objective c — Differentiate primary from secondary bacterial infection of the skin
set2.q: How does a cutaneous abscess differ in origin from a furuncle?
opts: An abscess arises from an obstructed apocrine gland, whereas a furuncle follows a break in the epidermis
Apocrine obstruction is the mechanism of hidradenitis suppurativa.
An abscess arises from lymphatic spread of streptococci, whereas a furuncle spreads along the dermis
Neither mechanism is described that way.
An abscess usually follows traumatic inoculation of bacteria, whereas a furuncle arises from an infected follicle
Correct. Abscesses are often polymicrobial, with Staphylococcus aureus the commonest organism.
An abscess arises from an infected hair follicle, whereas a furuncle follows traumatic inoculation of bacteria
That reverses the two mechanisms.

set2.io: Objective a — Etiologies, epidemiology, risk factors, manifestations, differential diagnosis, testing, management, referrals, education and prognosis for cutaneous bacterial infections
set2.q: Which organism causes erythrasma and where does it live?
opts: Staphylococcus aureus, releasing epidermolytic toxins that split the epidermis
That mechanism produces bullous impetigo.
Corynebacterium minutissimum, invading the upper third of the stratum corneum
Correct. Heat and humidity are the favourable conditions; diabetics are high risk.
Candida albicans, colonising the space beneath a separated proximal nail fold
That is the organism of chronic paronychia.
Pseudomonas aeruginosa, entering the follicle from inadequately chlorinated water
That organism causes hot tub folliculitis.

set2.io: Objective a — Etiologies, epidemiology, risk factors, manifestations, differential diagnosis, testing, management, referrals, education and prognosis for cutaneous bacterial infections
set2.q: What is the pharmacologic treatment of erysipelas?
opts: Penicillin V, with clindamycin if the patient is penicillin allergic
Correct. Prompt treatment matters because progression can be rapid.
Cephalexin, with trimethoprim-sulfamethoxazole if purulence is present
That regimen belongs to cellulitis.
Mupirocin ointment, with oral dicloxacillin if lesions are widespread
That regimen belongs to impetigo.
Doxycycline, with benzoyl peroxide added to reduce bacterial resistance
That combination belongs to acne vulgaris.

set2.io: Objective a — Etiologies, epidemiology, risk factors, manifestations, differential diagnosis, testing, management, referrals, education and prognosis for cutaneous bacterial infections
set2.q: Which lesion type is characteristic of hidradenitis suppurativa on examination?
opts: The tense clear bulla that leaves a collarette after rupture
That is bullous impetigo.
The double comedone — a blackhead with two or more openings
Correct, alongside nodules, sinus tracts, abscesses and meshlike scarring.
The honey-coloured adherent crust overlying a superficial erosion
That is non-bullous impetigo.
The follicular pustule pierced by a single central hair shaft
That is folliculitis.

set2.io: Objective a — Etiologies, epidemiology, risk factors, manifestations, differential diagnosis, testing, management, referrals, education and prognosis for cutaneous bacterial infections
set2.q: What is hidradenitis suppurativa and where does it occur?
opts: Infection of the hair follicle extending into the adjacent subcutaneous fat of the neck and back
That describes a furuncle.
Inflammation of cutaneous apocrine glands, most often in the axilla, and also groin, breasts or perineum
Correct. It is also called acne inversa because it resembles acne vulgaris.
Inflammation of the eccrine sweat glands, most often on the palms, soles and the axillary vault
Eccrine glands are the ones involved in hyperhidrosis, not this condition.
Infection of the upper third of the stratum corneum in intertriginous skin under heat and humidity
That describes erythrasma.

set2.io: Objective a — Etiologies, epidemiology, risk factors, manifestations, differential diagnosis, testing, management, referrals, education and prognosis for cutaneous bacterial infections
set2.q: Which finding in a woman with persistent acne points toward polycystic ovarian syndrome?
opts: Flushing with hot drinks and visible facial telangiectasias
That points toward rosacea instead.
Pustules pierced by a central hair over the thighs and trunk
That points toward folliculitis.
Premenstrual flares of acne with an otherwise normal cycle
Premenstrual flares are a common feature of ordinary acne.
Hirsutism together with irregular or absent menses
Correct. That combination indicates androgen hypersecretion.

set2.io: Objective a — Etiologies, epidemiology, risk factors, manifestations, differential diagnosis, testing, management, referrals, education and prognosis for cutaneous bacterial infections
set2.q: Where do furuncles and carbuncles typically occur?
opts: In areas prone to friction or minor trauma — back of neck, face, axillae and buttocks
Correct. Shaving and insect bites are named traumatic risk factors.
In intertriginous areas kept warm and moist — inner thighs, scrotum and toe webs
That is the distribution of erythrasma.
In areas bearing apocrine glands — axilla, groin, breasts and perineum
That is the distribution of hidradenitis suppurativa.
On the lower extremity in the great majority of cases, rarely bilateral
That is the distribution of cellulitis and erysipelas.

set2.io: Objective a — Etiologies, epidemiology, risk factors, manifestations, differential diagnosis, testing, management, referrals, education and prognosis for cutaneous bacterial infections
set2.q: Which three factors predispose to recurrent furunculosis?
opts: Obesity, diabetes and nasal carriage of Staphylococcus aureus
Correct. Immunocompromise and trauma are the broader risk categories.
Smoking, hot weather and obstruction of the apocrine ducts
Those are predisposing factors for hidradenitis suppurativa.
Impaired lymphatic drainage, tinea pedis and previous impetigo
Those are risk factors for erysipelas.
Manicure, ingrown nail and the habit of biting the nails
Those are predisposing factors for acute paronychia.

set2.io: Objective a — Etiologies, epidemiology, risk factors, manifestations, differential diagnosis, testing, management, referrals, education and prognosis for cutaneous bacterial infections
set2.q: What is the pathophysiology of pseudofolliculitis barbae?
opts: Keratin plugs occlude the pilosebaceous unit and sebum accumulates behind the blockage
That describes the follicular hyperkeratinisation of acne.
Apocrine ducts become obstructed and rupture, seeding inflammation into the dermis
That describes hidradenitis suppurativa.
A cut hair curves into the follicular wall and penetrates the skin, causing a foreign body reaction
Correct. It occurs in any shaved area and commonly in Black males with tightly curled facial hair.
Bacteria enter the follicle through a break in the skin and produce a follicular pustule
That is infectious folliculitis rather than this foreign body reaction.

set2.io: Objective a — Etiologies, epidemiology, risk factors, manifestations, differential diagnosis, testing, management, referrals, education and prognosis for cutaneous bacterial infections
set2.q: Why does devitalised tissue in cellulitis require surgical debridement?
opts: It prevents accurate culture of the organism from the affected area
Culture yield is not the reason debridement is required.
It causes pain that cannot be controlled with systemic analgesia
Pain control is not the stated indication.
It is not perfused, so antibiotics cannot reach the site
Correct — tense, cyanotic, necrotic, bronzed or blanched skin is the clue.
It harbours resistant organisms that no oral antibiotic will cover
The problem is delivery of the drug rather than resistance.

set2.io: Objective a — Etiologies, epidemiology, risk factors, manifestations, differential diagnosis, testing, management, referrals, education and prognosis for cutaneous bacterial infections
set2.q: Which statement about preventing hot tub folliculitis is correct?
opts: Showering immediately after contact reliably prevents it if done within thirty minutes
Showering afterwards is specifically stated not to prevent infection.
Raising the water temperature above forty degrees kills the organism responsible
Temperature is not the control measure described.
Wearing a rash guard in the water prevents the organism reaching the follicles
Barrier clothing is not among the preventive measures given.
Showering after contact does not prevent it; continuous filtration and disinfectant monitoring do
Correct, along with frequent changing of the water.

set2.io: Objective b — Unique considerations of methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus skin infections
set2.q: Which trait is shared by the oral agents named across this lecture for methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus skin infection?
opts: Penicillin V, erythromycin and clarithromycin recur as the core options
Those cover streptococcal and corynebacterial infection.
Mupirocin, retapamulin and fusidic acid recur as the core options
Those are topical agents rather than oral ones.
Trimethoprim-sulfamethoxazole, clindamycin and doxycycline recur as the core options
Correct, with linezolid and ciprofloxacin added in particular settings.
Dicloxacillin, cephalexin and amoxicillin-clavulanate recur as the core options
Those are the agents for methicillin-sensitive disease.
